source.title: Goal-directed hippocampal theta sweeps during memory-guided navigation

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed Nature Neuroscience paper, large-scale recordings, with a stated circuit mechanism (CA1 egocentric-goal-direction subpopulation + reduced feedback inhibition) and an explicit link between the online (theta) and offline (SWR) generative modes MECH-289 already distinguishes -- directly on-target for MECH-289's claim that the same generative hippocampal substrate operates in both modes. Full text accessed via PMC mirror (preprint), giving more confidence than an abstract-only read; the peer-reviewed Nature Neuroscience version was not independently checked for changes from the preprint.
failure_signatures: This is a preprint-derived summary (PMC12407861 mirrors the bioRxiv version, DOI 10.1101/2025.08.26.672489); the published Nature Neuroscience version (DOI 10.1038/s41593-026-02364-3) may differ in details not captured here.

Learning-dependence is explicitly part of the finding (goal-directed sweeps are described as learning-dependent, distinct from a stereotypic left-right alternating sweep type) -- this paper does not claim ALL theta sweeps are goal-directed, only a learned subpopulation, a distinction REE's claims should not flatten.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In rats performing memory-guided navigation, hippocampal place-cell sequences within theta cycles come in two kinds: a stereotypic left-right alternating sweep, and a distinct, learning-dependent goal-directed sweep that predicts the animal's upcoming trajectory toward a remembered goal. These goal-directed sweeps are coordinated with prefrontal cortex activity and are preferentially replayed during sharp-wave ripples (SWR). Mechanistically, a subpopulation of CA1 cells encodes egocentric goal direction, and reduced feedback inhibition is proposed as part of the circuit basis for generating these goal-directed sweeps.
mapping.ree_translation: Directly grounds MECH-289's claim that the hippocampal SWR trajectory generator operates as one generative substrate across both 'online (theta-analog)' and 'quiescent (offline, SWR-analog)' modes -- this paper is the first evidence this session found that explicitly links theta-cycle goal-directed sweeps to preferential SWR replay in the SAME learned content, rather than treating them as unrelated phenomena. Also supports MECH-236's goal-conditioning premise via the CA1 egocentric-goal-direction subpopulation finding, complementing Yu et al.'s dissociation-design evidence for the same premise.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The learning-dependence qualifier matters: this is not evidence that ALL hippocampal trajectory generation is goal-directed by default, only that a distinct, experience-dependent subpopulation becomes so -- MECH-289's anti-recency/generative claim and MECH-236's goal-conditioning claim should be read against this learned-subpopulation structure, not a blanket claim about the whole hippocampal sequence-generation apparatus. Same spatial-navigation-to-abstract-cognition transfer-risk caveat as the other entries in this directory; does not speak to SD-098's node-type-storage question.
mapping.source_context: Rats, large-scale hippocampal + prefrontal cortex electrophysiological recordings during memory-guided open-field navigation.

confidence_components.notes: Full-text (preprint, via PMC mirror) accessible, giving a fuller methodological picture than abstract-only. Mapping fidelity is good for MECH-289's dual-mode (theta/SWR) generative-substrate claim specifically -- this is the most directly on-target paper in the cluster for that claim. Transfer risk unchanged from the rest of the directory (rat spatial navigation vs. REE's abstract action-object/possibility-topology space).
